chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Isma'il from Khirash from Zurarah from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both)
Regarding four men who testified against a woman for adultery, one of them being her husband, he said: 'The husband performs li'an (mutual cursing), and the others are flogged.'
Therefore, acting upon the first report is preferable because it agrees with the apparent meaning of the Quran.
Allah the Exalted said: 'And those who accuse their wives [of adultery] and have no witnesses except themselves - then the testimony of one of them is four witnesses by Allah...'
Thus, it indicates that li'an is permissible if the man has no witnesses other than himself.
As for when he brings the witnesses who complete the four, then li'an is not obligatory upon him.

key_terms.شَهَادَةُ: Testimony or witnessing, specifically referring to the requirement of four witnesses for proving adultery.
key_terms.ظَاهِرِ الْقُرْآنِ: The apparent/literal meaning of the Quran, referring to the direct textual evidence used to derive the ruling.
key_terms.لِعَانُ: Li'an (mutual cursing), a specific judicial procedure in Islamic law where a husband accuses his wife of adultery without witnesses, involving oaths and curses.
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: He is flogged, referring to the punishment (hadd) for those who provide testimony but fail to prove the charge fully or are part of the group.

ai.seo_question: When is li'an obligatory versus when is it not required for a husband accusing his wife of adultery?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the juristic preference for the first report, which aligns with the apparent meaning of the Quran, by distinguishing between the specific case of li'an (where the husband's testimony suffices) and general zina accusations requiring four witnesses. This distinction clarifies that the obligation of li'an is lifted when the accuser produces the requisite four witnesses, shifting the penalty to flogging for the other parties. The hadith thus reinforces the principle of following the text that best corresponds to the Quranic explicitness in legal derivations.
